trigger: irreversible/merge-gate (security CI gate) + cross-module consumers (compliance A5.8 probe, CI-gate guard)

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the gate now fails closed whenever the prompt scan did not really run
doubts.disproof_attempt: In PR (diff) mode, prompt_injection_scan.py get_changed_files() returns [] on ANY git failure. The script then writes a well-formed {"findings": []} and exits 0. outcome=success, the file is non-empty and has a findings array, so the gate goes GREEN even though nothing was scanned. The same applies to per-file exceptions, swallowed per file. The report carries no files_scanned field. Not a regression (green before too), but the same 'crashed scan read as 0' class; the AC20 wording reads broader than what the code covers.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Make the diff failure fatal in the scanner, or reword the AC, doc and comment to say the guard covers a step failure or a missing/unusable report only, and file the diff-mode silent-[] case as a follow-up.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: docs/security-ci-setup.md: this invariant is enforced going forward by the CI-gate guard check (c)
doubts.disproof_attempt: check (c) only requires a `! -[fs] prompt_risks.json` test coupled to an exit plus no silent jq fallback. A future edit that turns the `*)` branch into a warning or drops the jq shape check would pass the guard; only shared/tests/test_security_prompt_risks_gate.py catches that. The doc sentence overstates what the guard enforces.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Reword the doc to say the guard enforces the missing/empty-report half and the behaviour test pins the rest.

doubts.disproof_attempt: The case block cannot tell an `if:`-false skip from a skip caused by an upstream failure. Safe today: the gate has no `if:` so it runs only under success(). If someone later adds `if: always()` to the gate, a crash before the prompt scan would turn into a warning-only skip.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Add a comment on the gate step saying it must keep the implicit success() condition, or have the guard reject `if: always()` on the gate step.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: a healthy scan always yields outcome=success
doubts.disproof_attempt: True today: no --fail-on is passed, so the scanner exits 0 even with findings. If someone adds `--fail-on high` to the scan step, outcome becomes failure on any high finding and the gate blocks on highs. A latent trap, not a current defect.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: A one-line comment on the scan step: no --fail-on here; a non-zero exit is read by the gate as a crash.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the compliance A5.8 behaviour probe keeps checking the gate
doubts.disproof_attempt: Nothing breaks: the `${{` sits in step env, not the run body; clean/critical fixtures stage a valid prompt_risks.json with PROMPT_SCAN_OUTCOME unset (strict path). But A5.8 has no scenario with a clean findings.json and a missing or corrupt prompt_risks.json, so the new behaviour is audited only by the repo test.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Optional: add such a scenario, or state that it is accepted as covered by shared/tests.

summary: No high doubts. No way found for a crashed prompt scan that leaves no usable report to go green, and no way for a healthy run to go red today. One medium remains: in PR mode a failed git diff silently produces a clean report, which still passes green; not a regression. Four lows cover doc/guard overclaim, skip ambiguity, the --fail-on trap and the A5.8 coverage gap.
